clue.text: Support for a French line of chocolate biscuits?

definitions.text: Support for a French line of chocolate biscuits?

parts.words: Support for a French line of chocolate biscuits?
parts.note: the French royal line shares its name with a chocolate sandwich biscuit, so loyalty to that dynasty is jokily recast as backing for a brand of biscuit

explanation.surface: Someone champions one particular range of chocolate biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bourbon is a British chocolate cream biscuit, and the Bourbons were the French royal dynasty; the question mark flags the pun on 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ism makes a word for adherence, here loyalty to the royal house that ruled France.

clue.text: The sort of sports in which an aristocratic rowdy appears

definitions.meaning: field sports in which animals are killed
a dated word for a wild young man of noble birth, a buck

explanation.surface: A well-born hooligan turns up at a hunting event.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting is called by this term, and in Regency slang a dashing rake of good family was one.

clue.text: Showing disrespect, unlike Frederic the apprentice

definitions.meaning: lacking proper obedience to parents or superiors
Frederic, apprenticed to pirates in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera, is the 'slave of duty'

explanation.surface: A rude youth is nothing like a famously conscientious trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederic is the hero of The Pirates of Penzance, whose sense of obligation is absurdly rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing in obligation to elders is disrespectful, the opposite of a character ruled by his sense of obligation.

clue.text: It shows how striker is doing in state time

definitions.text: It shows how striker is doing

parts.note: in cricket a side that is in is batting
to aver is to state firmly
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A footballer's form is reported, in a time of national crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests football; here it is the batsman, and 'in' is cricket's word for batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs scored divided by dismissals measures a batsman's performance.

clue.text: Foster goes on train to children's home

indicators.note: goes on places the word for foster in front of the railway letters

parts.note: to foster is to nurse or nurture
RY is short for railway, the train line

explanation.surface: A foster parent travels by train to an orphanage.
explanation.definitionFit: A room or school for young children, where they are cared for.

clue.text: Part of Bangladesh, as translated from the Hindu writings

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A passage from Bangladesh is translated from Hindu scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred treatise of Hinduism, a text of instruction or law.

clue.text: It shows the pitch is almost fissured

indicators.note: almost tells us to drop the final letter of the word for split

parts.note: fissured means split, cleft

explanation.surface: A groundsman notes that the cricket pitch is nearly cracked open.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical stave's opening symbol fixes which notes the lines stand for, so it sets the register.

clue.text: Anita, blonde at last, is free

parts.note: Anita Loos, the American writer of Gentlemen Prefer Blondes

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A fair-haired Anita is finally at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blonde' nods to Anita Loos's famous novel but only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Untied or unconfined, at liberty, is a synonym.

clue.text: Swimming race for the open title.

definitions.meaning: a race in which any stroke may be used, in practice front crawl
read as two words, a style or title that is unrestricted

explanation.surface: A swimming event is staged for an open championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors may choose any stroke in that event, and an unrestricted form of name is a free style.

clue.text: A future overspill town in Northants?

definitions.text: A future overspill town in Northants?

parts.words: A future overspill town in Northants?
parts.note: a Northamptonshire market town designated to take overspill population from London; 'overspill' also hints at water welling up

explanation.surface: Planners name a Midlands town to take people moving out of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Northants is Northamptonshire, an English Midlands county; in the 1960s this town was chosen to expand with London overspill.
explanation.definitionFit: The Northamptonshire market town was designated an expanded town for London's surplus population.

clue.text: This midshipman is more senior.

parts.note: naval slang for a junior officer with longer service than his fellows; the comparison suggests a word built on 'older'

explanation.surface: One young naval officer outranks another.
explanation.walkthrough: In the old Royal Navy, a midshipman of some years' standing was called by this name, as against a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an elderly person, and was naval slang for a long-serving midshipman.

clue.text: A submarine commander points to the plant

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel
N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: A naval officer indicates a particular plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A windflower is a garden flower of the buttercup family.

clue.text: People desperately tired before end of shift cause harm

indicators.note: desperately suggests the letters of the next word are thrown about wildly

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Workers worn out at the close of a long shift do damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' rearranges 'tired'; the people go after that although the clue names them first, and 'end of' takes the last letter of 'shift'. 'cause' is only a link, so 'harm' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage or loss is a synonym, as in 'to the detriment of'.

clue.text: Loses order and valuable deposit

indicators.note: order, as a verb, asks the letters of the preceding word to be put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone loses a bank order and a valuable deposit too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' suggests banking; here it is the geological sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine wind-blown silt laid down in thick beds makes very fertile soil, hence valuable.

clue.text: Soldiers in France return in muddle

annotationWithheld.why: Soldiers in France return in muddle (5): BEF (British Expeditionary Force) + OG, but OG needs 'return' to be both the word GO (a turn) and its reversal indicator; one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Soldiers in France return in muddle

clue.text: Psalm a bit unorthodox for such a religious rite

indicators.note: unorthodox suggests the letters of the preceding words are arranged unconventionally

explanation.surface: A psalm sung a little irregularly at a christening.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to christening, the rite of admission to the Church with water.

clue.text: Shilly-shally, giving answers that are poles apart

definitions.meaning: the two opposite replies, assent and refusal

explanation.surface: Someone dithers, giving opposite answers by turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying one thing then the other is vacillation, and the positive and negative replies are opposites.

clue.text: "Wash your hands, put on your " (Macbeth)

parts.note: Lady Macbeth's sleepwalking scene, where she tells her absent husband to wash and dress for bed

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's tragedy with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Act 5 of Macbeth the sleepwalking Lady Macbeth says 'Wash your hands, put on your nightgown; look not so pale.'
explanation.definitionFit: A loose garment worn in bed completes the quotation from the sleepwalking scene.

clue.text: Staff at wine cellar is for the high jump

parts.note: a staff is a long rod, a pole
a vault is an underground cellar for wine

explanation.surface: Employees caught at the wine cellar are in for severe punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the high jump' is British idiom for being in serious trouble; here it is the athletic event, and 'Staff' means a rod, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: The event where athletes clear a bar using a flexible rod is a high leaping event.

clue.text: Sort out a Continental muddle

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
a snarl is a tangle or muddle

explanation.surface: Untangling a European mess.
explanation.definitionFit: To untangle or disentangle something knotted is to sort it out.

clue.text: The sort of paint to harden on an article

parts.note: to temper steel is to harden it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Paint applied to toughen a manufactured item.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium in which pigment is bound with egg yolk, used by early painters.

clue.text: It is wheeled under a railway vehicle

definitions.text: It is wheeled under a railway vehicle

parts.words: It is wheeled under a railway vehicle
parts.note: a wheeled undercarriage truck pivoting beneath a carriage, with 'wheeled' suggesting being pushed around

explanation.surface: Something is pushed along beneath a train carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A swivelling wheel truck under a locomotive or carriage carries its weight on curves.

clue.text: It used to have a divine circulation

definitions.text: It used to have a divine circulation

parts.words: It used to have a divine circulation
parts.note: in Greek myth the fluid flowing in the veins of the gods; 'circulation' hints at a newspaper's readership

explanation.surface: Something, perhaps a religious paper, once enjoyed a heavenly readership.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek myth held that an ethereal fluid, not blood, ran through the gods' veins.

clue.text: Governor to welcome swell

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of a colonial governor
ave is a Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: The governor sets out to greet a dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise and fall, as the sea does, is to surge upward.

clue.text: About the first of March, the Prince of Darkness becomes a good man

indicators.note: About tells us the devil's name goes around the date

parts.note: the Prince of Darkness is Satan
the date written as MAR I, March's abbreviation plus the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: On the first of March, the devil reforms into a kindly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first of March' looks like M; it is the date written MAR I, which goes inside SATAN.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable, a Samaritan is anyone who kindly helps a stranger in need.

clue.text: One ship blowing up its hooters

indicators.note: blowing up suggests the letters are blasted apart and reassembled

parts.note: SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A ship explodes, its sirens sounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' is a link; hooters are the ship's sirens on the surface, slang for noses in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooters is British slang for a person's nostrils and the organs that carry them.

clue.text: Cry of surprise by small boy, say, with a muscular pain

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: say signals that the boy's name is wanted only for how it is pronounced

parts.note: Algy, short for Algernon, is a boy's name, made small by shortening

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a little lad who has a muscle ache.
explanation.walkthrough: Algy is the familiar short form of Algernon; 'say' wants only its sound, spelt here with an I. 'with' is a link, and 'a' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term from Greek myos, muscle, and algos, ache, names an aching muscle.

clue.text: Jealous bird stands over unfinished insect

indicators.note: stands over places the bird ahead of the insect in the entry

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: unfinished says the insect loses its last letter

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: A resentful bird stands guard over a half-dead bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means eager to rival or outdo another, hence envious of their success.

clue.text: Ship's back showing national emblem

indicators.note: back asks the ship's part to be read from end to start

parts.note: the ship's keel, the spine along the bottom of its hull

explanation.surface: The stern of a ship flies the flag of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' suggests the stern; it turns the keel round. 'showing' is a link. The national emblem is that of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh adopt this onion-family vegetable as a national symbol, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: Land she can distribute, having clear conscience

indicators.note: distribute tells us to share out and rearrange the letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A landowner can share out her estate with nothing on her conscience.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands unstained by guilt is the idiom for innocence of wrongdoing.
